headline: No dip to buy: BTC $84.9K on a $710M liquidation squeeze, 96% of it shorts
summary: There is nothing on sale right now. Bitcoin ran from an $81,164 open to an $85,428 high and sits at $84,940, with ETH at $2,723.97 and SOL at $116.79, and the fuel was forced short covering rather than spot demand - just over $710m of positions were liquidated in 24 hours across roughly 135,000 traders, and in the peak hour about $300m went, ~96% of it short side ($226m bitcoin, $59m ether). The trigger was technical and external, not crypto-specific: bitcoin's first weekly close above its 50-week average in 45 weeks, Brent crude falling for a fourth straight session on hopes that UN General Assembly diplomacy can defuse the US-Iran war, and S&P futures up over 0.5%. Underneath, the macro has not improved - the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September and Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said today the Fed is in an 'action scenario' and may need to hike faster if inflation is demand-driven. Sentiment is Greed (composite 64.5, Fear & Greed 70, BTC +9.8% / ETH +9.2% / SOL +15.3% on the week) while the 24h news tone reading is still negative at -0.73, and Reddit has flipped to open euphoria. That combination is a chase-or-wait tape rather than a bounce setup.

BTC.note: At $84,940 after covering its whole $80,394-$85,428 day range and reclaiming the $82,225 US spot-ETF cost basis for the first time since January; Hyperliquid funding is a modest 0.0016%/h (~0.04%/day) on $3.82bn open interest, so the squeeze has not yet produced crowded long financing.

ETH.note: At $2,723.97 and +9.2% on the week with about $59m of ether shorts liquidated in the peak hour, but it carries the weakest fund sponsorship of the three - US spot ether ETFs snapped a four-week inflow streak in the week to 18 September - even as Bitmine added 27,562 ETH at $2,727.

SOL.note: At $116.79 and the strongest of the three at +15.3% on the week, with the highest futures premium (0.094%) and funding of 0.0023%/h on a much smaller $720m Hyperliquid book, and Alpenglow mainnet activation on 28 September as asset-specific event risk.

drivers.title: The move is a short squeeze, not spot accumulation
drivers.detail: Just over $710m of crypto positions were liquidated in 24 hours across nearly 135,000 traders, and in the most recent hour about $300m went with roughly 96% on the short side - $226m bitcoin and $59m ether. The proximate trigger was bitcoin's first weekly close above its 50-week moving average in 45 weeks, which pushed price back through the $82,225 average cost of US spot ETF buyers; that is forced buying plus a technical level, not evidence of new cash entering.

drivers.title: Goolsbee hardened the hiking message today
drivers.detail: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, speaking in London, said supply shocks 'have come more frequently, hit harder and lasted longer', that the Fed is now more in an 'action scenario', and that rates may have to rise more aggressively if the inflation is demand-driven - pointing at services and the AI investment boom. This is the first voter commentary since the FOMC voted 12-0 on 16 September to raise the funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, its first hike in over three years and the first under Chair Kevin Warsh, with 16 of 18 SEP participants expecting at least one more hike in 2026. The stored history flags this exact topic: 'inflation/CPI' headlines preceded a BTC dip within 6h 2.6% of the time versus 1.0% by chance (2.67x lift, n=117).

drivers.title: Today's bid is borrowed from oil, and the war is not over
drivers.detail: Brent fell for a fourth consecutive session as traders watched Washington-Tehran diplomacy, and that is what lifted equity futures and crypto together. But Iran has said it will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the US lifts the naval blockade, eases sanctions and unfreezes assets, and President Pezeshkian only addresses the UN General Assembly on Tuesday - so the risk premium crypto is currently not paying can be put back on with a single headline.

drivers.title: Treasury companies keep buying, but well below spot
drivers.detail: Strategy filed an 8-K at 12:00 UTC today disclosing 950 BTC bought for about $76m between 14 and 20 September - its first purchase in weeks, taking the pile back toward its June record - while Strive added 1,355 BTC for $107.7m and Bitmine bought 27,562 ETH at $2,727 (~$75.2m), lifting it to 5,983,940 ETH or about 4.9% of supply with roughly 85% staked. Tom Lee framed it as institutions being underweight crypto after AI stocks outperformed early in 2026. Note that this is accumulation done at or under current price, not chasing.

drivers.title: ETF flow is thin and ether has turned
drivers.detail: US spot bitcoin ETFs finished the week to 18 September with just $6.2m of net inflow, salvaged entirely by a $433m Friday led by Fidelity's FBTC ($310.7m) against BlackRock's IBIT ($108.4m); for the full week IBIT took $120.7m and FBTC $79.9m while the rest of the category lost about $194.4m. Spot ether funds snapped a four-week inflow streak in the same week. The category is still roughly $1.45bn net negative year to date, so the passive bid is not what is driving this tape.

drivers.title: Rulemaking replaces legislation, and the ECB moves on tokenisation
drivers.detail: With the CLARITY Act dead on a 49-50 cloture vote on 15 September, the SEC and CFTC are now writing the US market-structure rules themselves - CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said the agency is 'locked in and ready to ship rules' under existing authority, and the SEC's conditional five-year exemption window for tokenised securities pilots opens 22 September. In parallel the ECB announced today that the Eurosystem will bring central bank money to tokenised finance via Pontes and that the ECB will invest part of its own funds in tokenised securities. This is plumbing that reduces tail risk rather than a flow event; it does not bid spot this week.

watch.what: Iranian President Pezeshkian addresses the UN General Assembly - the single biggest headline risk to the falling-oil bid underneath today's tape. The SEC's tokenised-securities exemption window also opens, TON unlocks 1.3% of supply (~$51.2m), and Messari Mainnet NYC runs 22-24 September.
Xi Jinping enters the United States ahead of the summit; Humanity unlocks 14.7% of supply (~$20.8m).

US initial jobless claims for the week to 19 September (consensus 201K) - the first labour read since the hike, and the inflation/data channel that historically preceded BTC dips at 2.7x the base rate. Trump hosts Xi at the White House the same day, with tariff cuts on non-strategic goods, an AI incident-notification mechanism and Chinese agricultural and Boeing purchases on the table.

Deribit quarterly BTC and ETH options expiry, around $16.6bn notional - the largest mechanical volatility source of the week. Plasma (XPL) also unlocks roughly 1.76-1.81bn tokens (~63-65% of circulating supply, ~$158m). US durable goods orders land 12:30 UTC and final Michigan sentiment 14:00 UTC.
Solana's Alpenglow mainnet activation, the largest protocol change of the quarter for SOL, following the 18 September cut in block time to 250ms.

Q3 ends and the SEC fiscal year closes on 30 September. For context on any pullback: the stored history says BTC dips during greed recovered +1.5% in 7 of 7 cases, ETH 92.9% of 28 and SOL 93.8% of 48, with typical extra drop after the trigger of -0.3% to -0.5%; but today's market state most resembles 2025-07-10, 2025-06-10 and 2024-07-22, after which BTC's median 30-day move was -3.0% (up in 50.0% of them).
